AS 15 — Employee Benefits.back: Contribution plan: employee bears actuarial and investment risk; employer's duty ends with the contribution. Benefit plan: employer bears both. A provident fund with a guaranteed return is a defined BENEFIT plan.

AS 15 — Employee Benefits.front: Other long-term employee benefits (long-service leave, jubilee awards)?
AS 15 — Employee Benefits.back: Measured like defined benefit plans, but simpler: actuarial gains and losses AND past service cost are both recognised immediately.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: Primary and secondary segment formats — what decides?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: The dominant source and nature of RISKS AND RETURNS. Mainly products and services: business segments primary, geographical secondary — and vice versa. Internal organisation and reporting is normally the guide.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: The 10% tests for a reportable segment?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Any ONE: revenue (external + inter-segment) ≥ 10% of total segment revenue; OR result ≥ 10% of the combined result of all segments in profit or all segments in loss, whichever is GREATER in absolute amount; OR assets ≥ 10% of total segment assets.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: Segment revenue — what is included and excluded?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Includes sales to external customers and inter-segment sales, directly attributable or reasonably allocable. Excludes extraordinary items, interest and dividend income (unless a financial segment), and gains on sale of investments.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: What must you do if reportable segments' combined external revenue is less than 75% of the entity's external revenue?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: 75%: Add additional segments (by descending revenue) until combined external revenue of reportable segments ≥75% of entity's external revenue.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: Disclosures for each PRIMARY reportable segment?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Revenue (external and inter-segment separately), result, carrying amount of assets, LIABILITIES, capital expenditure, depreciation and amortisation, other significant non-cash expenses. Segment liabilities are mandatory under AS 17.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: What reconciliations are mandatory between segment totals and entity financials?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Reconcile: total segment revenue, total segment result, total segment assets (and liabilities if disclosed) to the entity's corresponding totals; disclose unallocated items and reconciling adjustments.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: What must an entity disclose about how it identifies and measures segments?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Disclose: basis/factors used to identify segments (products, geography, regulation, customers), and measurement policies and bases for allocating revenue, expenses, assets, depreciation and inter-segment pricing.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: Segment result test when some segments are in loss?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Add up the profits of all segments in profit; add up the losses of all segments in loss. Take the LARGER total (absolute). A segment is reportable if its own profit or loss is 10% or more of that figure.
Measured on the basis the enterprise actually used to price them. Disclose that basis and any change in it.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: AS 17 approach vs Ind AS 108 — the exam trap?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: AS 17 identifies segments by RISKS AND RETURNS. The 'management approach' and 'chief operating decision maker' belong to Ind AS 108 — do not use them in an AS answer.

Extraordinary items, interest expense (unless a financial segment), losses on sale of investments, income tax, and general administrative and head-office expenses that relate to the enterprise as a whole.

AS 17 — Segment Reporting.front: A segment was reportable last year but falls below 10% this year?
AS 17 — Segment Reporting.back: Keep reporting it if management judges it to be of continuing significance. A segment reportable for the first time: restate prior-period comparatives unless impracticable.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: The five categories of related parties under AS 18?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: (a) Enterprises that control, are controlled by, or are under common control with the reporting enterprise. (b) Associates and joint ventures. (c) Individuals with control or significant influence, and their relatives. (d) Key management personnel and their relatives. (e) Enterprises over which (c) or (d) have significant influence.

Control: more than one-half of voting power, OR control of the board's composition, OR a substantial interest (20% or more) plus power to direct financial/operating policies. Significant influence: participation in those policy decisions without control — presumed at 20% or more of voting power.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: Key management personnel and 'relative' under AS 18?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: KMP: those with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities (MD, whole-time directors). A non-executive director is not KMP merely by being a director. Relative: spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, mother.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: What minimum items AS 18 requires for every related‑party transaction disclosure?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Nature of relationship, amount of transactions, outstanding balances (including commitments), terms (price, security, interest), provisions for doubtful debts, and amounts written off/forgiven. (AS 18 disclosure requirements)

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: Should related‑party disclosures be aggregated by class or shown per individual party under AS 18?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Disclose amounts aggregated by class of related party (e.g., subsidiaries, associates, KMP); name individual related parties only when necessary for understanding or when transactions are material. (AS 18)

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: No price was charged for the transaction — still disclosable?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Yes. A related party transaction is a transfer of resources or obligations REGARDLESS of whether a price is charged. AS 18 does not ask you to certify arm's length.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: Where control exists but there were no transactions?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Still disclose the NAME of the related party and the NATURE of the relationship. Control relationships are disclosed irrespective of transactions.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: Who is deemed NOT to be a related party?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Two companies merely having a common director; a single customer, supplier, franchiser, distributor or agent on whom the business depends economically; providers of finance, trade unions, public utilities and government departments in normal dealings.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: How must remuneration to Key Management Personnel be disclosed under AS 18?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Aggregate amount of remuneration to KMP must be disclosed (not necessarily per individual), and the relationship of close family members where relevant. (AS 18)

Intra-group transactions in CONSOLIDATED statements; transactions between state-controlled enterprises; and where disclosure would conflict with a duty of confidentiality under statute or a regulator (e.g. banks).
An individual or enterprise holding 20% or more of the voting power, directly or indirectly.

AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.front: Remuneration paid to a whole-time director — is that a related party transaction?
AS 18 — Related Party Disclosures.back: Yes — he is key management personnel, so the remuneration is disclosed. Sitting fees to a non-executive director are not (he is not KMP).

AS 19 — Leases.back: Ownership transfers at the end; bargain purchase option; lease term covers the major part of economic life; PV of minimum lease payments is substantially all of fair value; asset is so specialised that only the lessee can use it without major modification.

AS 19 — Leases.front: Finance lease in the lessee's books — amount and discount rate?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Asset and liability at the LOWER of fair value and PV of minimum lease payments (lessee's view). Discount at the rate implicit in the lease if practicable to determine; otherwise the lessee's incremental borrowing rate.

AS 19 — Leases.front: Over what period should a lessee depreciate a finance‑leased asset?
AS 19 — Leases.back: 2 cases: if ownership or bargain purchase option transfers — over economic life; otherwise — over the shorter of lease term and economic life. Residual value normally nil unless guaranteed. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: What is the lessor's accounting treatment at inception of a finance lease?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Derecognise underlying asset; recognise receivable equal to net investment (PV of minimum lease payments plus unguaranteed residual); unearned finance income = gross minus net investment, allocated by effective interest method. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: How are operating lease payments recognised by lessee and lessor?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Straight‑line rule: lessee recognises lease payments as expense on straight‑line basis unless another systematic basis is more representative; lessor recognises lease income similarly, retaining the asset. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: What exactly are 'minimum lease payments' under AS 19?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Includes payments over lease term, any bargain purchase option price, and any residual value guaranteed by lessee or related parties; excludes contingent rentals and service costs. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: How are contingent rentals and penalties for early termination treated?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Recognise contingent rentals and termination penalties as income/expense in the period they arise; they are not included in minimum lease payments. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: How is the lease term determined when renewal/termination options exist?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Lease term = non‑cancellable period plus renewal periods reasonably certain to be exercised and periods covered by termination options reasonably certain not to be exercised. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: Gross investment, net investment and unearned finance income?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Gross investment = minimum lease payments (lessor's view) + unguaranteed residual value. Net investment = gross investment − unearned finance income (i.e. its present value at the implicit rate).

AS 19 — Leases.front: Estimated unguaranteed residual value falls during the lease?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Review regularly. Revise the income allocation over the remaining term, and recognise IMMEDIATELY any reduction in respect of amounts already accrued.

AS 19 — Leases.front: What minimum future‑payments disclosures are required under AS 19?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Disclose aggregate future minimum lease payments under non‑cancellable operating leases by <1 year, 1–5 years, and >5 years, and present value of minimum lease payments for finance leases. (AS 19).

AS 19 — Leases.front: Sale and leaseback resulting in a FINANCE lease?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Any excess OR deficiency of sale proceeds over carrying amount is deferred and amortised over the lease term in proportion to depreciation of the leased asset. Nothing is taken to P&L at once.

AS 19 — Leases.front: Sale and leaseback resulting in an OPERATING lease?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Sale at fair value: profit/loss immediately. Below fair value: immediately — unless the loss is compensated by below-market future rentals, then defer. Above fair value: defer the excess over fair value. If fair value is below carrying amount, that loss is recognised at once.

AS 19 — Leases.front: Manufacturer or dealer lessor — finance lease?
AS 19 — Leases.back: Recognise selling profit as for an outright sale. If an artificially low interest rate is quoted, restrict profit to what a commercial rate would give. Initial direct costs: expense at the inception of the lease.
Leases to explore for or use natural resources (oil, gas, timber, minerals); licensing agreements for films, plays, manuscripts, patents, copyrights; and lease agreements to use LAND.

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: Give the Basic EPS formula and what is deducted from profit for its numerator.
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Basic EPS = (Profit attributable to equity shareholders − preference dividends) ÷ weighted average equity shares outstanding. Deduct preference dividend attributable to period. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: How do you compute the weighted average number of equity shares for the period?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Time‑weight shares outstanding for the reporting period; include shares issued during the year pro rata to time outstanding. Adjust for share buybacks/issuances accordingly. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: How must bonus issues and stock splits be treated when presenting EPS for prior periods?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Retrospectively adjust prior periods' share counts as if the bonus issue/stock split occurred at the start of earliest period presented; numerator remains unchanged. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: State the treasury‑stock method used for options, warrants and similar instruments for diluted EPS.
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Assume exercise; incremental shares = shares issued − shares repurchased using proceeds (exercise price×shares) at average market price during period. Include only if dilutive. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: How are convertible debt instruments adjusted in diluted EPS (numerator and denominator)?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Add back after‑tax interest saved (interest×(1−tax rate)) to numerator; add shares issuable on conversion to denominator, weighted for time. Include only if dilutive. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: How are convertible preference shares treated in basic and diluted EPS?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Basic: deduct preference dividend from numerator. Diluted: add shares on conversion to denominator and add back preference dividend to numerator (since dividends would cease on conversion). (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: What is the rule for identifying and treating anti‑dilutive potential ordinary shares?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Exclude potential ordinary shares that are anti‑dilutive — those that would increase basic EPS (for profit) or reduce loss per share (for loss). Only include instruments that reduce EPS. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: Presentation and disclosure of EPS under AS 20?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Basic AND diluted EPS on the face of the P&L for each class of equity, with equal prominence — even if negative. Also EPS excluding extraordinary items. Disclose the numerators with a reconciliation to net profit, weighted average shares, and nominal value per share.

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: Rights issue with a bonus element — the adjustment?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Theoretical ex-rights price = (fair value of all shares before rights + rights proceeds) ÷ shares after rights. Factor = fair value per share before rights ÷ theoretical ex-rights price. Multiply the pre-rights shares (and prior years') by the factor.

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: What is the correct order of steps and a common exam mistake when computing diluted EPS?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Compute Basic EPS first; then adjust numerator (after‑tax interest/dividends) and denominator for conversions; lastly apply treasury method for options. Common error: omitting tax effect on interest. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: How should cumulative versus non‑cumulative preference dividends be treated for Basic EPS?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Deduct cumulative preference dividends from profit attributable to equity shareholders whether paid or not; deduct non‑cumulative preference dividends only if declared/paid in the period. (AS 20).

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: Partly paid shares in the weighted average?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Counted as a FRACTION of a share, to the extent they are entitled to participate in dividend relative to a fully paid share.

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: Share application money pending allotment — basic or diluted?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: Not in basic EPS. If it is not statutorily required to be kept separately and is being used in the business, treat it as dilutive POTENTIAL equity shares for diluted EPS.

AS 20 — Earnings per Share.front: Several potential equity instruments — in what order are they tested?
AS 20 — Earnings per Share.back: From MOST dilutive to least dilutive (lowest earnings per incremental share first). Include one only if it lowers EPS from continuing ordinary operations; stop when the next would raise it.

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: A component that, under a SINGLE PLAN, is being disposed of substantially in its entirety, disposed of piecemeal, or terminated through abandonment — AND is a separate major line of business or geographical area — AND is distinguishable operationally and for financial reporting.

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: How are the assets of a discontinuing operation measured?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: AS 24 has NO measurement rules — it is a presentation and disclosure standard. Apply the other standards: AS 28 for impairment, AS 29 for provisions, AS 10, AS 15. ('Held for sale at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs' is Ind AS 105.)

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: Initial disclosure event — what triggers the disclosures?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: The EARLIER of: a binding sale agreement for substantially all the assets of the operation; or the Board approving a detailed formal plan AND announcing it.

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: What goes on the FACE of the P&L for a discontinuing operation?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: Pre-tax profit or loss from its ordinary activities and the related tax expense; and the pre-tax gain or loss on disposal of its assets or settlement of its liabilities. Not a single net-of-tax line.

Description of the operation, its segment, date and nature of the initial disclosure event, expected completion; carrying amounts of total assets to be disposed of and liabilities to be settled; its revenue and expenses; net cash flows by operating, investing, financing.

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: What is NOT a discontinuing operation?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: Gradual phasing out of a product line; discontinuing several products within an ongoing line; shifting production or marketing to another location; closing a facility to save costs; selling a subsidiary whose activities are similar to the parent's.

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: What principal disclosures about the nature and timing of disposal does AS 24 require?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: Disclose: nature of operation, expected manner and timing of disposal, carrying amounts, revenue, pre‑tax results and tax effects (AS 24).

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: How are cash flows of a discontinued operation presented under AS 24?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: Separate disclosure: net cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities attributable to the discontinued operation (AS 24).

AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.front: The plan is later withdrawn, or continues into next year?
AS 24 — Discontinuing Operations.back: Withdrawn: disclose that fact and its effect. Continuing: update the disclosures every period up to and including the period in which the discontinuance is completed. Comparatives are restated to segregate the operation.

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: What is the primary objective of AS 25 interim reporting that you must state in one line in the exam?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Provide a timely update on material events and changes since the last annual financial statements so users can make economic decisions (objective of AS 25).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: Minimum components of an interim financial report (AS 25)?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Condensed balance sheet, condensed statement of profit and loss, condensed cash flow statement, and selected explanatory notes. (There is no statement of changes in equity under AS.)

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: Which two dates must the condensed balance sheet compare?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: 2 dates: end of current interim period and end of immediately preceding financial year (comparative balance-sheet requirement).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: What profit & loss comparatives must you show for interim reporting?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: 4 comparatives: current interim period, year-to-date current period, comparable interim period of previous year, year-to-date comparable period of previous year (present both single-period and YTD comparatives).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: What accounting-policy rule applies to interim financial statements?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Use the same accounting policies as the most recent annual financial statements; disclose any change and its effect on the current interim and year-to-date amounts (consistency requirement).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: How must income tax expense be determined for interim periods?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Apply an estimated average annual effective tax rate to the year-to-date pre-tax profit or loss, allocating tax to the interim period (tax allocation rule for interim reporting).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: Seasonal revenue and uneven costs at an interim date?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Do NOT anticipate or defer them at the interim date unless that would also be appropriate at the year-end. Test: would it be recognised if this were the annual balance sheet date?

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: How must material non‑recurring or unusual items be presented in interim reports?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Disclose nature and amount of material non-recurring or unusual items separately for the interim and year-to-date periods (separate disclosure requirement).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: Change in accounting policy vs change in estimate during the year?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Policy: restate the PRIOR INTERIM periods of the current financial year. Estimate: earlier interim figures are not restated; a significant change in the final interim period is disclosed in the annual statements.

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: How is materiality judged in an interim report?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: In relation to the INTERIM period's financial data — not the forecast annual figures. Interim measurements may rely more on estimates.

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: When must a condensed cash flow statement be included in an interim report?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Include a condensed cash flow statement year-to-date if the entity presents a cash flow statement in its annual financial statements; otherwise it may be omitted (cash-flow inclusion rule).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: What interim disclosures about seasonal or cyclical operations are mandatory?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Describe the nature and financial effect of seasonal or cyclical variations that materially affect interim results (seasonality disclosure requirement).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: What must be disclosed about events occurring after the interim period end?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Disclose material events after the interim period end that could affect users’ decisions, explaining their nature and estimated financial effect (post‑period events disclosure).

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: Does frequency of reporting change the annual result?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: No. Interim measurement is on a YEAR-TO-DATE basis, so quarterly or half-yearly reporting must give the same annual figures. Same accounting policies as the annual statements.

AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.front: Year-end bonus, and inventories, at an interim date?
AS 25 — Interim Financial Reporting.back: Bonus: anticipate only if there is a legal or constructive obligation and a reliable estimate. Inventories: same principles as year-end; write down to NRV at the interim date. Basic and diluted EPS go on the face of the interim P&L.

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: What is 'current tax' and how is it measured under AS 22 at balance-sheet date?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Current tax: tax payable under the Income-tax Act, measured using tax laws and rates enacted at the balance-sheet date; recognised as current tax expense and current tax liability/asset. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: What gives rise to deferred tax and how is it measured?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Deferred tax arises from timing differences between taxable income and accounting profit; measured at tax rates and laws enacted at the balance-sheet date. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Which timing differences require recognition of deferred tax liabilities?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: All taxable timing differences: recognise deferred tax liabilities in full. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Recognising deferred tax ASSETS — the prudence tests?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Normally: REASONABLE CERTAINTY of sufficient future taxable income. Where there is unabsorbed depreciation or carried-forward tax losses: VIRTUAL CERTAINTY supported by convincing evidence (e.g. firm orders in hand).

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Is deferred tax recognised on a revaluation surplus of fixed assets?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Revaluation surplus: no deferred tax is recognised on revaluation surplus of fixed assets until realised. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Tax rate changes — which rate, and where does the effect go?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Measure at rates and laws enacted or substantively enacted by the balance sheet date. The effect of a change is taken to the PROFIT AND LOSS of that year.

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: When may you offset deferred tax assets and liabilities in the balance sheet?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Offsetting allowed only when a legally enforceable right exists to set off current tax assets and liabilities and both deferred tax items relate to the same taxation authority. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Should deferred tax assets and liabilities be discounted to present value?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Do not discount deferred tax assets or liabilities; measure at nominal amounts. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: When should deferred tax be recognised and when reversed?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Recognise deferred tax in the same period the timing differences originate; reverse deferred tax when the timing difference reverses. (AS 22)

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Timing vs permanent differences — exam examples?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Timing: depreciation (book vs tax), section 43B items allowed on payment, provision for doubtful debts, preliminary expenses. Permanent: penalties and donations disallowed, exempt income — no deferred tax.

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: What minimum disclosures does AS 22 require in the financial statements?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Disclose components of tax expense, current tax payable, movements in DTA/DTL, and reasons for unrecognised deferred tax assets. (AS 22)
Timing differences that reverse DURING the holiday: no deferred tax. Those that reverse AFTER it: recognise in the year they originate. Assume those that originate first reverse first.

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: MAT and MAT credit under AS 22?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: MAT paid is CURRENT tax. MAT credit is not a deferred tax asset: recognise 'MAT credit entitlement' as an asset only on convincing evidence that normal tax will be payable within the set-off period.

AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.front: Deferred tax assets at each balance sheet date?
AS 22 — Accounting for Taxes on Income.back: Review the carrying amount: write down if realisation is no longer reasonably/virtually certain; reverse the write-down if it becomes so. Reassess unrecognised deferred tax assets too.

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: State the recognition test for an intangible asset under AS 26 – what minimum must be satisfied to capitalise it?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: 2 criteria: (1) probable future economic benefits; (2) cost can be measured reliably. Both must be met to recognise an intangible asset (AS 26 recognition rule).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: What items are included in the initial cost of an intangible asset?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Purchase price plus directly attributable expenditures to bring the asset to use (e.g., legal fees, testing). Subsequent general overheads excluded unless directly attributable (AS 26 measurement on initial recognition).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: How are internally generated Intangibles treated — research vs development?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Research costs expensed; development costs capitalised only if 6 criteria are satisfied (technical feasibility, intention, ability to use/sell, probable future benefits, resources available, reliable measurement) (AS 26).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: When does amortisation of an intangible asset begin and what is the usual residual value assumption?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Amortisation begins when the asset is available for use. Residual value is normally zero unless a contractual commitment or market exists to recover it (AS 26 amortisation start and residual value).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: How often must useful life and amortisation method be reviewed and how are changes accounted?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Review useful life and amortisation method at least annually; changes prospectively as a change in accounting estimate (AS 26 review and adjustment rule).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: Useful life of an intangible asset under AS 26?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Rebuttable presumption: not more than TEN years from when it is available for use. Every intangible is amortised — there is no 'indefinite life, no amortisation' under AS. If amortised over more than 10 years: disclose why, and test for impairment every year.

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: Can an intangible asset be revalued under AS 26?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: No. Cost less accumulated amortisation and impairment only. The revaluation model for intangibles is Ind AS 38.

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: When can subsequent expenditure on an existing intangible be capitalised?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Capitalise only if it meets recognition criteria and increases future economic benefits; otherwise expense. Routine maintenance and day-to-day servicing are expensed (AS 26 subsequent expenditure).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: How is an intangible asset acquired in exchange measured when the exchange has no commercial substance?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: If exchange lacks commercial substance and fair value not reliably measurable, measure acquired asset at carrying amount of asset given up; otherwise use fair value (AS 26 exchange provision).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: What is the accounting on derecognition (disposal) of an intangible asset?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Recognise gain or loss in P&L equal to net disposal proceeds minus carrying amount on disposal or retirement (AS 26 derecognition rule).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: What minimum disclosures AS 26 requires annually for each class of intangible assets?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Disclose opening carrying amount, additions, disposals, revaluations, amortisation, impairment losses, and closing carrying amount, plus amortisation methods, useful lives, and revaluation details (AS 26 disclosure requirements).

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: What can NEVER be recognised as an intangible asset?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Internally generated goodwill, brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists. Expensed when incurred: research, start-up and preliminary costs, training, advertising, relocation.

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: Expenditure on an intangible item was expensed last year — can it be capitalised now?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: No. Expenditure initially recognised as an expense cannot be reinstated as part of the cost of an intangible asset later.

AS 26 — Intangible Assets.front: Amortisation method, and intangibles not yet in use?
AS 26 — Intangible Assets.back: Method should reflect the pattern of benefits; if that cannot be determined reliably, STRAIGHT-LINE. An intangible not yet available for use is tested for impairment at least every year-end.

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: When is an asset treated as impaired under AS 28?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: When carrying amount exceeds recoverable amount. Impairment loss = carrying amount − recoverable amount (AS 28).
The HIGHER of net selling price (arm's-length sale price less costs of disposal) and value in use (present value of future cash flows from use and eventual disposal).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: What are the three required steps to estimate value in use?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: 3 steps: estimate future cash inflows/outflows; select a pre‑tax discount rate reflecting time value and asset‑specific risks; discount cash flows to present value (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: Which discount rate is used to compute value in use?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: A pre‑tax discount rate that reflects the time value of money and risks specific to the asset or CGU (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: When must impairment be tested at cash‑generating unit (CGU) level rather than individually?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: Test at CGU where an asset does not generate largely independent cash inflows; CGU = smallest identifiable group generating largely independent inflows (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: What is the order for allocating an impairment loss within a CGU?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: 2 steps: reduce allocated goodwill first; then allocate remaining loss pro‑rata to other assets of the CGU, without reducing any asset below its recoverable amount (AS 28).
Inventories (AS 2), assets arising from construction contracts (AS 7), financial assets including investments (AS 13), and deferred tax assets (AS 22).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: Reversing an impairment loss — when, the cap, and goodwill?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: Only if the ESTIMATES used for recoverable amount have changed. Cap: the carrying amount (net of depreciation) had no loss been recognised. Goodwill: reversed only if the loss came from a specific external event of an exceptional nature and later external events reversed it.

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: How is impairment of an asset carried at revalued amount treated?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: Impairment reduces revaluation surplus for that asset to the extent of any credit balance in revaluation reserve; any excess impairment recognised in profit or loss (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: Name four external indicators that an asset may be impaired.
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: 4 indicators: significant fall in market value; adverse changes in market, economy or legal environment; rising market interest rates; market capitalisation below carrying amount (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: Name four internal indicators that an asset may be impaired.
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: 4 indicators: physical damage or obsolescence; worse‑than‑expected asset performance; plans to discontinue or restructure use; internal evidence of obsolescence or underperformance (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: What is the single most common calculation mistake students make on impairment of depreciable assets?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: Failing to revise future depreciation after recognising impairment. Correct: allocate impairment, then recalculate remaining depreciable amount and depreciate prospectively over revised remaining life (AS 28).

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: Cash flow estimates for value in use — the rules?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: Based on reasonable assumptions and approved budgets, normally up to FIVE years. Exclude financing cash flows and income tax, and the effects of future restructuring not yet committed or future capital expenditure that enhances performance.

AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.front: Goodwill and corporate assets in a CGU test?
AS 28 — Impairment of Assets.back: Bottom-up test: can it be allocated to the CGU on a reasonable basis? If yes, test that CGU including it. If not, also do a top-down test on the smallest larger CGU to which it can be allocated.

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: State the three conditions required to recognise a provision under AS 29.
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: 3 conditions: present obligation from a past event, probable outflow (more likely than not), and a reliable estimate of the amount. (AS 29 recognition criteria).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Give the exam definition of a 'provision' under AS 29 in one line.
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Present obligation of uncertain timing/amount arising from a past event, recognised because a probable outflow and reliable estimate exist. (AS 29 definition).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: When is a contingent liability recognised or merely disclosed under AS 29?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Not recognised; disclose unless the possibility of outflow is remote. If obligation is only possible or outflow is not probable, treat as contingent liability and disclose. (AS 29).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Contingent asset under AS 29 — recognise, disclose, or neither?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Not recognised AND not disclosed in the financial statements. If an inflow is probable, it is usually mentioned in the Board's report. When realisation becomes VIRTUALLY CERTAIN it is no longer contingent — recognise it.

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: How must the amount of a provision be measured under AS 29?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Best estimate of the outflow at the reporting date, reflecting risks and uncertainties; use expected value for large populations. (AS 29 measurement).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Are provisions discounted to present value under AS 29?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: NO — except decommissioning, restoration and similar liabilities recognised as part of the cost of PPE, which are discounted at a pre-tax rate. General discounting is IAS 37 / Ind AS 37.

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Expected reimbursement (insurance, indemnity) of a provision?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Recognise only when VIRTUALLY CERTAIN, as a separate asset, not exceeding the provision. In the P&L the expense may be shown net of the reimbursement.

Only when the ordinary recognition criteria are met — AS 29 does not recognise 'constructive obligations'. No obligation for a sale of an operation until there is a binding sale agreement. Include only direct costs, not ongoing activities.

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: When must an onerous contract give rise to a provision and how is it measured?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Provision where unavoidable costs to fulfil exceed benefits; measure as the lower of cost to fulfil the contract and cost of exiting it. (AS 29 onerous contracts).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Are provisions allowed for anticipated future operating losses under AS 29?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Prohibited: provisions for future operating losses are not allowed and must not be recognised. (AS 29 prohibition).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: How and when should provisions be reviewed and adjustments accounted for under AS 29?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Review at each reporting date; adjust provision to the current best estimate. Recognise increases or decreases in profit or loss. (AS 29).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Fast exam rule to distinguish provision, liability and contingent liability under AS 29.
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Provision = present obligation + probable outflow + reliable estimate (recognise). Liability = present and measurable. Contingent liability = possible obligation or improbable outflow → disclose, do not recognise. (AS 29).

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Probable, possible, remote — the three outcomes?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Probable (more likely than not) + reliable estimate: PROVIDE. Possible, or probable but not measurable: DISCLOSE as contingent liability. Remote: nothing.

AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.front: Measuring a provision — three things to remember?
AS 29 — Provisions, Contingent Liabiliti.back: Best estimate, before tax. Ignore gains from the expected disposal of assets. A provision is used only for the expenditure it was created for; reverse it if an outflow is no longer probable.
